item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hum. This works quite well for building up the tension for the events that are about to unfold, but as nonsensical as this is going to sound, I don't think that enough actually happens here. Of course, we're given quite a bit of insight on all kinds of hell (Or heaven) that's breaking lose, but the fact that this tale depicts so many different scenes that aren't directly connected to each other kind of limits how in-depth the reader gets to witness them, to me at least.

On the other hand, the characterization of Mann and Gears is great here, especially in regards to how the later appears only briefly, but that's enough to really convey how serious the situation is, given the previously established canon about his personality.

No vote.(Major points for craaaaaabs, though).

item.content:encoded: But the reason it's being claimed not to be as "enjoyable" is due to a misunderstanding about what the story segment is claiming. The context of the segment's content is then redefined by a later entry, rendering those objections null. Fine, I admit, someone could downvote it for those reasons and then refuse to change their vote even after learning the truth due to them not enjoying it the first time. But I personally would call that having a stick up their bum, being closeminded, and making assumptions.

item.content:encoded:
It feels like 343 was chosen to be God not because he worked well, but because he worked best. I don't think he works at all.

I chose 343 from several candidates; my original idea was to not use an SCP for "Yahweh" at all. Hell, my idea here doesn't match my own personal canon for what 343 is (and as I'm sure you know by now from reading the following entry, there is an explanation, at least).

Hopefully I can win you over (once you read future entries and maybe come back and see the setup?), but I also understand downvoting for being sick of 343. I'm sick of 343 too. I just really liked this idea.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Agreed. The entire POINT was to lead you to think that that was what the story was saying, and then part three twists it. This part would be weak perhaps if it were a single entry. But as part of a continuing storyline, it is not intended to be read on its own, nor should it be expected to be. The events in this section are defined by the events in the next section. This is not an SCP article, it cannot and should not be judged on its own merits alone.

This kind of objection is like reading one chapter from the middle of the book and complaining that it raises too many unresolved questions.
